value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Chino/San Bernardino County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Site plan, roof plan, structural calculations, and electrical plan (submitted online via the Citizen Access portal)
All manufacturer specification sheets, installation instructions, and U.L. listings, attached to the plans
Chino Valley Fire District approval (separate submittal, at 14011 City Center Drive, Chino Hills)
Partial roof framing plan showing new/existing rafters, beams, headers, spacing, sheathing, and roofing materials
Structural support calculations by a licensed professional engineer or architect (existing and proposed loads)
Lateral calculations by a licensed professional engineer or architect per 2022 CBC 3403.2.3.1#2 (existing lateral resisting elements no more than 10% overstressed)

value: Submit an inspection request through the City's online Request an Inspection form (permit number, site address, and inspection type required)
Inspections are conducted Monday through Friday, 8am-4pm; requests must be submitted before 3pm for next-day inspection
For additional information, contact the Development Services Department, Building Division at 909-334-3251
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.program_or_pathway: Standard electronic plan review (Solar Photovoltaic System Submittal Requirements, 2023)
other_conditions: Photovoltaic permit is only issued to contractor licensing classifications B, C-46, C-10, or qualified personnel with certification
Current code year (CBC, CRC, CEC) must be identified on plans

eligibility_constraints.notes: This document describes the city's standard plan-review submittal process, not a SolarAPP+/automated instant-permitting pathway — no evidence of a separate SolarAPP+ program was found for Chino this session (unlike neighboring Chino Hills).
